claims.text: An ML-accelerated thermodynamic-integration method can accurately calculate solid and liquid free energies.
The method can retain vibrational-entropy, anharmonic, and electron–vibration-coupling effects.
The method can reduce computational cost by at least one order of magnitude relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
The method can mitigate the severe slowdown encountered by TOR-TILD for multicomponent high-entropy systems.
Training data will consist of targeted ab initio configurations from both crystalline and liquid phases.
An ML interatomic potential will be trained on targeted ab initio data and used for enhanced-sampling thermodynamic integration.
The proposed integration will sample the phase spaces of both solid and liquid states.
The method is intended to apply from elemental and binary systems through multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The intended temperature window is approximately 0.9T_m to 1.1T_m.
The ML potential mediates the method by approximating the ab initio free-energy landscape.
Free-energy differences and entropy contributions can be faithfully reproduced through the learned energy surface.
Training on carefully selected snapshots from both phases inherently captures anharmonic effects.
Training on carefully selected snapshots from both phases inherently captures electron–vibration coupling.
Using the surrogate potential permits phase-space integration with fewer expensive ab initio molecular-dynamics steps.
Predicted free energies, fusion temperatures, and latent heats will be within roughly 5–10% of full ab initio molecular-dynamics results.
The method will be at least ten times faster than explicit ab initio workflows.
The proposed validity boundary excludes, or remains uncertain for, systems with extreme electronic or magnetic complexity.
Performance depends on the representativeness of the training set and its transferability across compositional regimes.
A deviation greater than approximately 10% in fusion temperature or free-energy differences from ab initio molecular-dynamics benchmarks will falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to reproduce the expected entropy contributions relative to established TOR-TILD results will falsify the hypothesis.
